thread.title: Amazon Stock To Benefit From Spinoff Of Web Services Unit?

author: BRIAN DEAGON
title: Amazon Stock To Benefit From Spinoff Of Web Services Unit?

organizations.name: amazon stock to benefit from spinoff of web services unit

text:
Amazon.com ( AMZN ) should split in two to avoid antitrust scrutiny and also increase shareholder value, said a Wall Street analyst Monday, who also reiterated a buy rating on Amazon stock.
X
Meanwhile, reports surfaced over the weekend that the e-commerce giant is investigating suspected data leaks and bribes of its employees.
Citi analyst Mark May thinks separating Amazon Web Services' cloud computing unit from its retail business makes sense given that President Donald Trump is "obsessed" with the e-commerce giant and could potentially go after the company on antitrust grounds. Trump has attacked Amazon multiple times and has argued that it has a "huge antitrust" problem .
May estimates a $600 billion enterprise value for AWS and $400 billion value for its retail business.
Minimizing Risks For Amazon Stock "There has been greater noise of late regarding the desire to investigate and potentially regulate the company," May wrote in a note to clients. "By separating the retail and AWS businesses, Amazon could minimize or avoid the risk of increased regulatory pressure."
Other reasons for splitting Amazon would be to achieve a better valuation and to avoid or minimize conflicts of interest, he wrote.
May maintained a buy rating on Amazon stock and a price target of $2,250. That's a 14% premium from where the stock currently trades. May last week raised his price target on Amazon to 2,250 from 2,100. He based that on the strength of the company's large and growing Amazon Prime membership program.
May estimates that Prime subscribers will more than double to 275 million in a decade.
Suspected Data Leaks, Bribes The Wall Street Journal on Sunday said Amazon is investigating suspected data leaks and bribes of its employees as it fights to root out fake reviews and other seller scams from its website.
The practice, which violates company policy, is particularly pronounced in China. Employees of Amazon are offering internal data and other confidential information that can give an edge to independent merchants selling their products on the site, the report said.
Shares of Amazon dropped 3.2% to close at 1,908.03 on the stock market today . Amazon stock is up 63% this year.
Amazon stock recently hit a record high of 2,050.50, making it the second company to touch the lofty threshold of $1 trillion in market value. Apple ( AAPL ), in early August, became the first company to reach the $1 trillion plateau.
